## Remarks

The negative algebraic tail is genuinely attractive at every allowed
separation; the hard core and lattice-shell summation give a uniform stability
constant. The example does not say that every attractive power tail is stable.
The A-page theorem remains a free-cube grand-pressure result and gives no
canonical fixed-density or arbitrary-boundary conclusion.

## Statement

For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The half-open cube $\Lambda_L$, a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, and, when the barycenter is used, a law $C_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$; use [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]].

[F1] [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]: $R_{L,\omega}$ averages the translations of the $L\mathbb Z^d$-periodic continuation over one fundamental cube.

[F2] [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]: stationarity means invariance under every translation and finite intensity means finite expected count in a unit cell.

[F3] [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]], and [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: $\Lambda_L$ has volume $L^d$, translations preserve Lebesgue measure, and nonnegative sums may be integrated termwise.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and definitions in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 By [F1], $R_{L,\omega}$ is the push-forward of normalized Lebesgue probability on $\Lambda_L$, so it is a probability measure. For a bounded measurable local $f$ and $y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$R_{L,\omega}(f\circ T_y)=L^{-d}\int_{\Lambda_L}f(T_{x+y}\omega^{(L)})\,dx.$$
The integrand is $L\mathbb Z^d$-periodic in $x$. The translated cube $\Lambda_L+y$ is another fundamental region for this lattice; partitioning it and $\Lambda_L$ into their finitely many translated intersections and using translation invariance of Lebesgue measure gives equal integrals. Hence $R_{L,\omega}(f\circ T_y)=R_{L,\omega}(f)$ for every $y$, so $R_{L,\omega}$ is stationary. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 For bounded Borel $A$, Tonelli's theorem and the periodic continuation give
$$R_{L,\omega}(N_A)=L^{-d}\int_{\Lambda_L}\sum_{q\in\omega}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}\mathbf1_A(q+Lk+x)\,dx.$$
For each fixed $q\in\omega$, the sets $\Lambda_L+Lk$ partition $\mathbb R^d$ up to null boundaries. Translating variables in each integral therefore makes the inner sum of integrals equal to $|A|$. Summing over the $N$ representatives gives $R_{L,\omega}(N_A)=N|A|/L^d$. Taking $A=[0,1)^d$ proves $\rho(R_{L,\omega})=N/L^d$ and finite intensity. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The barycenter $\bar C_L$ is a probability mixture of the stationary laws $R_{L,\omega}$, so it is stationary. By step 2.1 and Tonelli,
$$\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}[R_{L,\omega}(N_{[0,1)^d})]=E_{C_L}N/L^d<\infty.$$
Thus it belongs to the finite-intensity stationary domain of $\tau_L$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, probability measures, standard-Borel observation spaces where conditioning is used, and the exact finite-region relative entropy definition.

[A1] AC supplies Radon–Nikodym densities on these finite measure spaces and is required by the conditional density supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-radon-nikodym-density-exists-and-is-unique-up-to-almost-everywhere-equality]]).

[F1] For $P\ll Q$, $h=dP/dQ$ is nonnegative, $Q(h)=1$, unique almost everywhere, and $D(P\Vert Q)=Q(h\log h)$ ([[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]).

[F2] A joint density on a product of sigma-finite probability spaces produces an everywhere conditional probability kernel by dividing by its finite positive marginal density; zero and infinite marginal fibers are filled without division ([[thm-conditional-density-formula]]).

[F3] Nonnegative product-measurable functions have measurable section integrals and Tonelli iterated-integral equality ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

[F4] Dominated and monotone convergence justify the bounded truncation limits in the entropy integrals ([[thm-dominated-convergence]], [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]).

[F5] Natural logarithms turn products into sums and $\log 1=0$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]).

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and exact definitions in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 For $P\ll Q$ with density $h$, the negative part of $h\log h$ is integrable because $-u\log u\leq1/e$ for $0\leq u\leq1$; the density definition is therefore unambiguous. Also $u\log u\geq u-1$ for $u\geq0$, so $D(P\Vert Q)=\int h\log h\,dQ\geq\int(h-1)\,dQ=0$. If $P\not\ll Q$, the defined value is $+\infty\geq0$. [A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 For bounded $\phi$, let $Q_\phi$ have density $e^\phi/Q(e^\phi)$ relative to $Q$. When $P\ll Q$ and $D(P\Vert Q)<\infty$, the density logarithm identity gives $D(P\Vert Q_\phi)=D(P\Vert Q)-P(\phi)+\log Q(e^\phi)\geq0$ by step 1.1. Thus every variational test is at most $D(P\Vert Q)$; the same upper bound is immediate if $D=+\infty$. If $P\not\ll Q$, choose a measurable $Q$-null set $N$ with $P(N)>0$ and use $\phi=t\mathbf1_N$: then $Q(e^\phi)=1$ and $P(\phi)=tP(N)\to\infty$. [step 1.1, F1, F5, construct]

3.1 In the remaining case $P\ll Q$, let $h=dP/dQ$ and set $\phi_m=\max(-m,\min(m,\log h))$, taking $\phi_m=-m$ on $\{h=0\}$. Then $e^{\phi_m}\to h$ and $e^{\phi_m}\leq1+h$, so [F4] gives $Q(e^{\phi_m})\to1$. The negative part of $h\phi_m$ is bounded by $1/e$, and its positive part increases to $(h\log h)^+$; hence [F4] gives $P(\phi_m)=\int h\phi_m\,dQ\to D(P\Vert Q)$, including when the positive entropy part is infinite. Combining this with step 2.1 proves the variational identity. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F4, F5]

4.1 If $T$ is measurable, every bounded test $\psi$ on the target pulls back to the bounded test $\psi\circ T$ on the source, and $Q(e^{\psi\circ T})=(Q\circ T^{-1})(e^\psi)$ while $P(\psi\circ T)=(P\circ T^{-1})(\psi)$. Taking suprema in step 3.1 proves the restriction inequality. [step 3.1, F5]

4.2 Finiteness of $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)$ gives a joint density and its conditional kernel by [F2]. Pushing forward by $(s,y)\mapsto(r(s),y)$ and using step 4.1 gives finite $D(P_{R,Y}\Vert P_R\otimes Q_Y)$, so [F2] supplies the corresponding conditional kernel for $R$ as well. Thus all conditional densities and references in this clause are defined. For a conditioning observation $R$, applying the variational identity pointwise to the conditional density $k_R(r,y)$ shows $$G(R)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(E_P\phi(R,Y)-E_P\!\left[\log\int e^{\phi(R,y)}Q_Y(dy)\right]\right),$$ where the tests range over bounded measurable functions of $(R,Y)$. The upper bound follows from step 2.1 for each conditional law; the reverse bound follows by using the jointly measurable bounded truncations of $\log k_R$ from step 3.1 and then [F3]–[F4]. When $R$ is a measurable function of $S$, every test depending on $(R,Y)$ is an admissible test depending on $(S,Y)$ with the same objective value, since the $Q_Y$ normalizer still depends only on $R$. Thus $G(R)\leq G(S)$; nonnegativity is step 1.1 applied conditionally. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

5.1 Suppose $P_{XY}$ has density $h(x,y)$ relative to $Q_X\otimes Q_Y$. Put $h_X(x)=\int h(x,y)Q_Y(dy)$. By [F3], $h_X$ is a density for $P_X$. Where $0<h_X(x)<\infty$, [F2] supplies the conditional density $k(x,y)=h(x,y)/h_X(x)$ relative to $Q_Y$; elsewhere use its supplied filler. On the full $P_X$-measure set of finite positive $h_X$, $h=h_Xk$ and $\log h=\log h_X+\log k$ $P_{XY}$-almost everywhere. Integrating this identity, with nonnegative conditional entropies and finite total entropy, gives the displayed chain rule. If a restriction entropy is infinite, step 4.1 makes the joint entropy infinite as well, so no subtraction of two infinite terms is used. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 4.1, F5]

6.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove nonnegativity and the variational identity, step 4.1 proves restriction monotonicity, step 5.1 proves the product chain rule, and step 4.2 proves monotonicity under additional conditioning. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 4.2] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC and let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, with this class defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], be stationary for the translations of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a bounded Borel set $G$, write $P_G$ and $Q_G$ for the restrictions of $P$ and the unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q$ to configurations in $G$. For $L>0$, put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and
$$D_L:=D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
Then the specific relative entropy density
$$I(P):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D_L}{L^d}$$
exists in $[0,+\infty]$ and satisfies
$$I(P)=\sup_{m\in\mathbb N,\ m\geq1}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})}{m^d}.$$
If $I(P)<\infty$, every bounded Borel restriction has finite relative entropy. This is an information functional relative to the specified unit-intensity Poisson law; changing the reference changes its value.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, dimension $d\geq1$, a stationary finite-intensity configuration law $P$, and the unit-intensity reference $Q$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the standard-Borel Poisson reference and its countable product construction ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]).

[F1] For independent Poisson reference restrictions on disjoint bounded sets, the finite-region relative entropy is nonnegative, obeys the conditional chain rule, and does not increase under restriction ([[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]], [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]], [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]).

[F2] The domain $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$ consists of translation-invariant laws with finite unit-cell count, and stationarity of $P$ and $Q$ gives $D(P_{G+x}\Vert Q_{G+x})=D(P_G\Vert Q_G)$ for every bounded Borel $G$ and translation $x$ ([[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]]).

[F3] If a cube restriction has finite relative entropy, then every bounded subregion has no larger relative entropy ([[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]], claim 2).

## Proof

**Given:** AC, $P$, and $Q$ as in the Statement.

1.1 If $G_1,G_2$ are disjoint bounded Borel sets, [F1] decomposes $D(P_{G_1\cup G_2}\Vert Q_{G_1}\otimes Q_{G_2})$ into $D(P_{G_1}\Vert Q_{G_1})$ plus the mean conditional relative entropy of $G_2$ given $G_1$. That conditional increment is at least $D(P_{G_2}\Vert Q_{G_2})$ by the conditioning monotonicity in [F1], comparing observation by $G_1$ with no observation. Thus relative entropy is superadditive over disjoint regions; if the left side is infinite the inequality is immediate, and otherwise all terms in the chain rule are finite. [A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 Fix an integer $m\geq1$ and let $q_N=\lfloor N/m\rfloor$. Tile $[0,q_Nm)^d$ by $q_N^d$ disjoint translates of $\Lambda_m$, leaving the Borel remainder $\Lambda_N\setminus[0,q_Nm)^d$. Iterating step 1.1 and using nonnegativity on the remainder gives $$D(P_{\Lambda_N}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N})\geq q_N^dD(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m}),$$ because stationarity gives the same entropy for each translated $m$-cube. If $D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})=+\infty$, this forces $D(P_{\Lambda_N}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N})=+\infty$ for every $N\geq m$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Put $s=\sup_{m\geq1}m^{-d}D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})$. If $s=+\infty$, step 2.1 makes the liminf of $N^{-d}D_N$ exceed every finite bound, so the integer-cube limit is $+\infty=s$. If $s<+\infty$, step 2.1 gives $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}N^{-d}D_N\geq m^{-d}D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})$$ for every $m$, since $q_N^d/N^d\to m^{-d}$. Taking the supremum gives liminf at least $s$, while the definition of $s$ gives $N^{-d}D_N\leq s$ for every integer $N$. Hence the integer-cube limit exists and equals $s$. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For real $L\to\infty$, let $N=\lfloor L\rfloor$. The inclusions $\Lambda_N\subseteq\Lambda_L\subseteq\Lambda_{N+1}$ and [F3] give $D_N\leq D_L\leq D_{N+1}$. Since $N/L\to1$ and $(N+1)/L\to1$, step 3.1 squeezes $L^{-d}D_L$ to the same extended limit $s$; if some integer-cube entropy is infinite, monotonicity gives the same conclusion directly. [F2, F3, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 If $I(P)<\infty$ and $A$ is bounded, choose an integer cube $\Lambda_N+x$ containing $A$. Stationarity [F2] and restriction monotonicity [F3] give $$D(P_A\Vert Q_A)\leq D(P_{\Lambda_N+x}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N+x})=D(P_{\Lambda_N}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N})\leq N^d I(P)<\infty.$$ Thus every bounded restriction has finite relative entropy. [F2, F3, step 3.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let
$$\mathcal H_c:=\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega): I(P)\leq c\},\qquad c\in[0,\infty),$$
where $I$ and the local-tame topology $\tau_L$ are defined by [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. Then $\mathcal H_c$ is compact and sequentially compact in $\tau_L$. This is a pure measure-theoretic compactness theorem for simple locally finite configurations relative to the independent unit-intensity Poisson reference; it makes no thermodynamic-limit or physical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, HB, dimension $d\geq1$, and a finite $c\geq0$.

[A1] AC supplies the standard-Borel extension and the choice principles required by the local standard-Borel and Dunford–Pettis suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[A2] The ultrafilter extension principle gives Tychonoff compactness for arbitrary products of compact Hausdorff spaces; DC and HB supply the weak Eberlein–Šmulian equivalence ([[def-ultrafilter-extension-principle]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-hahn-banach-extension-principle-relative]]).

[F1] For every integer $m\geq1$, $I(P)=\sup_{m\geq1}m^{-d}D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})$ ([[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]]).

[F2] Relative entropy is nonnegative, decreases under restriction, and obeys its variational formula ([[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]], [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]).

[F3] On a finite measure space, a uniformly integrable family in real $L^1$ is relatively weakly compact, and relative weak compactness is equivalent to relative weak sequential compactness under the named choice hypotheses ([[thm-dunford-pettis-for-l-one-on-a-finite-measure-space]], [[thm-eberlein-smulian]]).

[F4] A product of compact Hausdorff spaces is compact under the ultrafilter extension principle, and consistent finite-dimensional laws on standard-Borel coordinate spaces extend to a unique probability law under AC ([[thm-compact-hausdorff-tychonoff-from-the-ultrafilter-lemma]], [[def-standard-borel-space]], [[thm-kolmogorov-extension-for-standard-borel-coordinate-spaces]]).

[F5] Under $Q$, a bounded-region count is Poisson and has finite exponential moment $E_Qe^{aN_A}=\exp(|A|(e^a-1))$ for every $a>0$ ([[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]], [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]).

[F6] A bounded measurable test defines a bounded linear functional on real $L^1(Q_W)$ by integration, using Hölder; it is therefore weakly continuous by the definition of the weak topology. Such tests separate distinct $L^1$ classes (test a nonzero difference against its measurable sign), so the weak topology is Hausdorff ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], [[def-weak-topology-on-a-normed-space]]).

[F7] Monotone and dominated convergence justify the nonnegative count truncations and the exponential-moment limit used below ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Let $W=a+[0,m)^d$ be any integer cube, with $a\in\mathbb Z^d$ and integer $m\geq1$. Translation invariance and [F1] give $D(P_W\Vert Q_W)\leq c|W|$. If $A$ is any bounded Borel set, choose one such cube $W$ containing it; by restriction monotonicity [F2], every $P\in\mathcal H_c$ satisfies $D(P_A\Vert Q_A)\leq C_A:=c|W|$. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

1.2 For any probability density $h$ relative to a probability $Q$ with $D(hQ\Vert Q)\leq C$, and any $K>1$, $$\int_{\{h>K\}}h\,dQ\leq\frac{C+1/e}{\log K}.$$ Indeed, $-u\log u\leq1/e$ on $[0,1]$, while $h\log h\geq h\log K$ on $\{h>K\}$. Split the entropy integral at $h=1$ and combine these bounds. Thus, for each fixed cube $W$, the densities $dP_W/dQ_W$ with $P\in\mathcal H_c$ have $L^1(Q_W)$ norm one and are uniformly integrable. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Fix $W$. By [F3], the weak closure $K_W$ of these densities in real $L^1(Q_W)$ is weakly compact. It is Hausdorff by [F6]. Every $h\in K_W$ remains nonnegative and has integral one: testing against each indicator and against $1$ gives weakly closed conditions by [F6]. Also $D(hQ_W\Vert Q_W)\leq c|W|$, because [F2] expresses $D$ as the supremum of weakly continuous affine functions of $h$, with continuity given by [F6]. Hence all entropy sublevels used below are closed in their local weak topologies. [A1, F2, F3, F6, step 1.2]

3.1 Index all integer cubes $W=a+[0,m)^d$ with $a\in\mathbb Z^d$ and integer $m\geq1$ by their countable set of pairs $(a,m)$, and form the product $K_*:=\prod_WK_W$. It is compact by [A2] and Hausdorff because each weak $L^1$ topology is Hausdorff by [F6]. Impose the following closed conditions on its tuples: whenever $W\subseteq V$, the $W$-marginal of $h_VQ_V$ equals $h_WQ_W$; and, for every real translation $x$ and bounded local measurable test $f$, the two marginals containing the supports of $f$ and $f\circ T_x$ satisfy $E_Pf=E_P(f\circ T_x)$. Each equality is closed because it tests weak convergence against bounded measurable functions on a containing cube, which are continuous by [F6]. The intersection $K_{\rm stat}$ of these closed conditions is compact. [A2, F6, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 A tuple in $K_{\rm stat}$ defines consistent finite-dimensional laws on the countable standard-Borel cell spaces: for a finite set of cells, choose any integer cube containing it and take that marginal. If two cubes contain the same finite set, a larger integer cube contains both; the imposed nested consistency makes their induced laws agree. By [F4] there is a unique law $P$ on $\Omega$ with those marginals. The imposed equalities make $P$ stationary, and each origin-anchored cube $[0,m)^d$ retains $D(P_{[0,m)^d}\Vert Q_{[0,m)^d})\leq c m^d$. Therefore [F1] gives $I(P)\leq c$. The extension map identifies $K_{\rm stat}$ with the set of laws having these local marginals and entropy constraints. [A1, A2, F1, F4, step 3.1]

5.1 The same variational inequality controls particle-count tails uniformly. Fix bounded $A$, choose $W\supseteq A$ as in step 1.1, and let $K\geq0$, $a>0$, and $M\in\mathbb N$. The bounded local test $\phi_M=a\min(N_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}},M)$ in [F2] gives $$aE_P\min(N_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}},M)\leq C_A+\log E_Q\exp(\phi_M).$$ As $M\to\infty$, monotone convergence yields $$aE_P[N_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}}]\leq C_A+\log E_Qe^{aN_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}}}.$$ By [F5] and dominated convergence the logarithmic term tends to zero as $K\to\infty$. First choose $a$ large and then $K$ large; this proves uniform integrability of the counts $N_A$ over every law in the closure family, and in particular finite intensity for its limit laws. [A1, F2, F5, F7, step 1.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 The product compactness in step 3.1 first gives compactness for all bounded local tests. For any tame $f$ supported in $A$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$, set $f_K=f\mathbf1_{\{N_A\leq K\}}$. Then $f_K$ is bounded and local, and its expectation is weakly continuous by [F6], while $$\sup_{P\in\mathcal H_c}|E_P(f-f_K)|\leq b\sup_{P\in\mathcal H_c}E_P[(1+N_A)\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}}]\longrightarrow0$$ by step 5.1. Thus on the entropy level the tame expectation maps are uniform limits of bounded-local continuous maps. Every $P\in\mathcal H_c$ supplies its cube densities and gives a tuple in $K_{\rm stat}$, so the extension map from $K_{\rm stat}$ is onto; the local expectations just shown make it continuous. Its image $\mathcal H_c$ is compact in $\tau_L$. [F6, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 Each $K_W$ is weakly compact in real $L^1(Q_W)$ and hence weakly sequentially compact by [F3]. Given a sequence in $K_{\rm stat}$, successively take subsequences converging in the first, second, and later cube coordinates and diagonalize; AC supplies the countable choices. The limit tuple preserves all closed consistency, stationarity, and entropy constraints from step 3.1, so it gives a law in $\mathcal H_c$ by step 4.1. Count-tail uniformity from step 5.1 upgrades coordinate convergence on bounded local tests to convergence for every tame test by the same truncation estimate in step 6.1. Hence $\mathcal H_c$ is sequentially compact in $\tau_L$. [A1, A2, F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The stated choice hypotheses, torus-invariant laws, and bounded entropy densities.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-ultrafilter-extension-principle]], [[def-dependent-choice]], and [[def-hahn-banach-extension-principle-relative]]: the explicit hypotheses for the local compactness, marginal extension and sequential compactness supplied by [F4].

[F1] [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] and [[lem-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field-stationary-density]]: the empirical field averages translations of the periodic continuation; its barycenter is stationary with intensity $E_{C_L}N/L^d$ when this expectation is finite.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]: relative entropy decreases under restriction, is superadditive over disjoint regions against a product reference, and satisfies the bounded-test variational inequality.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]]: Poisson counts have all positive exponential moments.

[F4] [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]: its local-density weak compactness, consistent marginal extension, and count-tail truncation argument apply under the named choice hypotheses to uniformly bounded entropy on every fixed cube.

[F5] [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]]: for a stationary law, $I(P)=\sup_{a\in\mathbb N}a^{-d}D(P_{[0,a)^d}\Vert Q_{[0,a)^d})$.

[F6] [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]] and [[thm-dominated-convergence]]: bounded count truncations may increase to counts, and Poisson exponential domination justifies the tail limits below.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 For bounded local $f$, torus invariance gives $E_{C_L}f(T_x\omega^{(L)})=E_{C_L}f(\omega^{(L)})$ for every $x$. Integrating over $\Lambda_L$ proves $\widetilde C_L(f)=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}(f)$. In particular the continued law is stationary. The entropy inequality with bounded truncations of $aN_{\Lambda_L}$ and [F3] gives finite $E_{C_L}N$, so the intensity assertion of [F1] applies. [given, F1, F2, F3, F6, algebra]

2.1 Fix an integer $a\geq1$ and take $L>a$. The fundamental cube contains $m_L=\lfloor L/a\rfloor^d$ disjoint translates of $W=[0,a)^d$. Their Poisson restrictions are independent and their $C_L$ marginals are identical by torus invariance. Superadditivity gives
$$D((\widetilde C_L)_W\Vert Q_W)\leq D(C_L\Vert Q_L)/m_L=c_LL^d/m_L.$$
For fixed $a$, $L^d/m_L\to a^d$. Translation invariance gives the same bound for every translate of $W$, hence a uniform entropy bound on every bounded region. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 On a bounded $A\subset W$, apply the entropy inequality to $t\min(N_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}},M)$ and let $M\to\infty$. If $C_W$ is the uniform bound from step 2.1, then
$$tE_{\widetilde C_L}[N_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}}]\leq C_W+\log E_{Q_W}e^{tN_A\mathbf1_{\{N_A>K\}}}.$$
For fixed $t>0$, the logarithm tends to zero as $K\to\infty$ by [F3] and [F6]. First take $t$ large and then $K$ large. This proves uniform count-tail integrability. The local weak-density compactness and consistent marginal extension in [F4] now give subsequential convergence for bounded local tests; the uniform tails upgrade it to $\tau_L$ convergence. Every limit is stationary. Lower semicontinuity of finite-region entropy and step 2.1 imply $a^{-d}D(P_W\Vert Q_W)\leq\liminf c_L$ for every integer $a$ along a subsequence realizing the liminf; [F5] proves the stated entropy bound. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 If the empirical fields converge in probability to $P_*$, then for bounded local $f$ the bounded random variables $R_{L,\omega}(f)$ converge in probability to $P_*(f)$, hence their expectations converge. By step 1.1 this is convergence of $\widetilde C_L(f)$. For tame $f$, truncate on $\{N_A\leq K\}$; step 3.1 makes the truncation error uniformly small, and the same is true for the limit law. Taking $L\to\infty$ and then $K\to\infty$ proves convergence for every stated tame observable. [F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, as defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], have finite specific relative entropy $I(P)=\gamma<\infty$ relative to the unit-intensity reference $Q$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Let $C=[0,1)^d$ be the reference cell and order the other unit cells lexicographically; $F_+$ is the set of cells preceding $C$. For each finite $A\subset F_+$ let $k_A$ be the conditional density of the configuration in $C$ given the configuration in $A$, relative to $Q_C$, as supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$g(A):=E_P[\log k_A]=D(P_{A\cup C}\Vert Q_{A\cup C})-D(P_A\Vert Q_A)$$
is finite, nonnegative, and increasing with finite $A$, with $\sup\{g(A):A\subset F_+\text{ finite}\}=\gamma$. For any increasing finite exhaustion $A_m\uparrow F_+$, the densities $k_{A_m}$ converge in $L^1(P_{F_+}\otimes Q_C)$ to a density $k_\infty$ of $P_{F_+\cup C}$ relative to $P_{F_+}\otimes Q_C$, and
$$\log k_{A_m}\longrightarrow\log k_\infty\quad\text{in }L^1(P).$$
The logarithmic convergence is directed: for every $\varepsilon>0$ some finite $A_m$ satisfies $\sup_{B\supseteq A_m,\ B\subset F_+\text{ finite}}E_P|\log k_B-\log k_\infty|<\varepsilon$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, dimension $d\geq1$, a stationary law $P$ with $I(P)=\gamma<\infty$, the cell partition and its lexicographic order.

[A1] AC is inherited from the Poisson reference construction and used by the conditional density and uniformly integrable martingale suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], [[thm-conditional-density-formula]], [[thm-uniformly-integrable-martingale-convergence]]).

[F1] For $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, finite specific entropy implies every bounded-region restriction has finite relative entropy; its normalized cube entropies converge to $\gamma$ ([[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]]).

[F2] Independent Poisson reference increments, the conditional entropy chain rule, its variational form, and monotonicity under added conditioning ([[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]], [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]).

[F3] A nonnegative uniformly integrable martingale converges almost surely and in $L^1$ ([[thm-uniformly-integrable-martingale-convergence]]).

[F4] On a probability space, uniform integrability plus convergence in probability implies $L^1$ convergence ([[thm-uniform-integrability-plus-probability-convergence-implies-l1-convergence]]).

[F5] Monotone convergence and Fatou apply to the nonnegative truncations and entropy densities used below ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[thm-fatou-lemma]]).

[F6] Agreement of finite measures on a generating pi-system implies agreement on the generated sigma-algebra ([[thm-dynkin-pi-lambda]]).

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Let $A\subset F_+$ be finite. By [F1], $D(P_{A\cup C}\Vert Q_{A\cup C})$ is finite, so the joint density $h_{A,C}$ relative to $Q_A\otimes Q_C$ exists. The marginal density $h_A$ is its $Q_C$ integral. On $0<h_A<\infty$, [F2] gives the conditional density $k_A=h_{A,C}/h_A$ relative to $Q_C$; the exceptional fibers have $P_A$-measure zero. The chain rule in [F2] gives $g(A)=E_P D(P_{C|A}\Vert Q_C)=D(P_{A\cup C}\Vert Q_{A\cup C})-D(P_A\Vert Q_A)$, so $g(A)$ is finite and nonnegative. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 If $A\subseteq B\subset F_+$ are finite, apply the conditional-increment monotonicity in [F2] to observation of the cell configuration on $A$ and then on $B$. It yields $g(A)\leq g(B)$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 To identify the supremum, let $\Lambda_N=[0,N)^d$, the union of $N^d$ unit cells, and order those cells lexicographically. Repeated use of the conditional chain rule decomposes $D(P_{\Lambda_N}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N})$ as the sum of $g(B_i)$ over its cells $i$, where $B_i$ is the finite set of earlier cells in $\Lambda_N$. Each $B_i$ is a finite subset of $F_+$ after translating cell $i$ to $C$, so $g(B_i)\leq\sup_Ag(A)$ by stationarity and step 2.1. Hence $D(P_{\Lambda_N}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N})/N^d\leq\sup_Ag(A)$. Conversely, fix finite $A\subset F_+$. For every cell $i$ in the inner cube whose distance from the boundary exceeds the largest coordinate magnitude in $A$, the translated set $i+A$ lies in $B_i$. By step 2.1 and stationarity, $g(B_i)\geq g(A)$. The proportion of these interior cells tends to one, and all other increments are nonnegative by step 1.1. Taking $N\to\infty$ and applying [F1] gives $\gamma\geq g(A)$. Taking the supremum over $A$ proves $\sup_Ag(A)=\gamma$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

5.1 For any finite-past cylinder event and any event in $C$, integrate $k_\infty$ over their product. $L^1(R)$ convergence makes this equal the limit of the same integral against $k_{A_m}$, which is the corresponding joint probability under $P$. ## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\geq1$, let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, with this class defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], be ergodic under the full translation group $\mathbb R^d$, and suppose its specific relative entropy $I(P)=\gamma$ relative to the unit-intensity Poisson law $Q$ is finite. Ergodic means that every measurable event invariant modulo $P$-null sets under each translation has probability $0$ or $1$. For an integer $N\geq1$, let $\Lambda_N=[0,N)^d$, and let $h_N=dP_{\Lambda_N}/dQ_{\Lambda_N}$, which exists because $D(P_{\Lambda_N}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_N})<\infty$. Then
$$\frac{1}{N^d}\log h_N\longrightarrow\gamma\qquad\text{in }L^1(P).$$
Without the full-translation ergodicity hypothesis the proof yields an invariant $L^1(P)$ limit of mean $\gamma$; it need not be constant.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a stationary finite-intensity law $P$, finite specific relative entropy $\gamma$, and ergodicity under every real translation.

[A1] AC is used by the conditional-density convergence and Hilbert-space mean-ergodic suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[lem-tdmath-conditional-log-density-convergence]], [[thm-von-neumann-mean-ergodic-theorem-in-l-two]]).

[F1] For $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, every bounded restriction has finite relative entropy when $I(P)<\infty$, the cube entropy ratio converges to $\gamma$, and the cube ratios are bounded above by $\gamma$ ([[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]]).

[F2] The conditional density of a unit cell given its finite past has logarithm with directed $L^1$ limit $Z=\log k_\infty$, where $k_\infty$ is a density relative to $R_0:=P_{F_+}\otimes Q_C$ and $E_PZ=\gamma$ ([[lem-tdmath-conditional-log-density-convergence]]).

[F3] Finite-region densities factor into successive conditional densities relative to the independent Poisson restrictions; the chain rule identifies the expectation of each conditional log density with its conditional relative entropy. If $k$ is a conditional density relative to a probability reference $R$, then $E_P(-\log k)^+=\int_{0<k<1}k(-\log k)\,dR\leq1/e$, because $u(-\log u)\leq1/e$ for $0<u<1$ ([[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]], [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]).

[F4] For each measure-preserving transformation, the Cesàro averages on complex $L^2$ converge in norm to the orthogonal projection onto its invariant subspace ([[thm-von-neumann-mean-ergodic-theorem-in-l-two]]).

[F5] On a probability space $L^2$ convergence implies $L^1$ convergence by Hölder, and dominated convergence passes integrable truncations to the limit ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Let $S_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$ be the cell indices in $\Lambda_N$. For $i\in S_N$, set $A_{i,N}=\{j-i:j\in S_N,\ j<_{\rm lex}i\}$; this is a finite subset of the past of the reference cell. Repeated conditional-density factorization from [F3] gives, $P$-almost surely, $$\log h_N(\omega)=\sum_{i\in S_N}\log k_{A_{i,N}}(T_{-i}\omega).$$ Every finite factor is defined $P$-almost surely because the corresponding local relative entropy is finite by [F1]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 Fix $\varepsilon>0$. By the directed convergence in [F2], choose a finite past $A_*$ such that every finite $B\supseteq A_*$ satisfies $E_P|\log k_B-Z|<\varepsilon$. Put $R=\max\{|a_j|:a\in A_*,1\leq j\leq d\}$, with $R=0$ if $A_*=\varnothing$. Let $S_N^\circ$ consist of cells at least $R$ cells from each face of $S_N$. If $i\in S_N^\circ$, then $A_*\subseteq A_{i,N}$, so by stationarity $E_P|\log k_{A_{i,N}}(T_{-i}\omega)-Z(T_{-i}\omega)|<\varepsilon$. The boundary has $N^d-(N-2R)^d=o(N^d)$ cells (for $N>2R$). For every finite past $B$, $E_P\log k_B=g(B)\leq\gamma$ and $E_P(-\log k_B)^+\leq1/e$, hence $E_P|\log k_B|\leq\gamma+2/e$. For $Z=\log k_\infty$, $E_P(-\log k_\infty)^+=\int_{0<k_\infty<1}k_\infty(-\log k_\infty)\,dR_0\leq1/e$ on its reference probability $R_0=P_{F_+}\otimes Q_C$, so [F2] gives $E_P|Z|\leq\gamma+2/e$ as well. Summing the interior errors and bounding each boundary error by $2(\gamma+2/e)$ yields $$\left\|N^{-d}\log h_N-N^{-d}\sum_{i\in S_N}Z(T_{-i}\cdot)\right\|_{L^1(P)}\longrightarrow0,$$ since $\varepsilon$ was arbitrary. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For $j=1,\ldots,d$, the shift $U_jf=f\circ T_{-e_j}$ is a linear isometry on complex $L^2(P)$ by stationarity. Apply [F4] to $N^{-1}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}U_j^n$, obtaining strong convergence to the orthogonal projection $P_j$ onto the $U_j$-invariant subspace. The coordinate shifts commute, so every average for coordinate $j$ commutes with every average for coordinate $k$; taking strong limits shows that the $P_j$ commute with each other and with the other coordinate averages. Since all these operators have norm at most one, a finite telescoping estimate gives strong convergence of the product of the $d$ averages to $P_1\cdots P_d$. This product is the orthogonal projection onto the intersection of the coordinate-invariant subspaces, because the $P_j$ are commuting orthogonal projections. The product averages are exactly the rectangular cube averages $N^{-d}\sum_{i\in S_N}Z_M(T_{-i}\cdot)$, so these converge in $L^2$ for bounded $Z_M$ to a function invariant under every integer shift. [A1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Since $Z\in L^1(P)$, dominated convergence gives $\|Z-Z_M\|_1\to0$. Cube averages are $L^1$ contractions, so the averages of $Z$ are Cauchy in $L^1$: for large $M$ their distance from the convergent averages of $Z_M$ is at most $\|Z-Z_M\|_1$. Let their $L^1$ limit be $s$. Every cube average has mean $E_PZ=\gamma$, hence $E_Ps=\gamma$. For each coordinate shift $e_j$, the averaging index cube and its translate have symmetric difference of exactly $2N^{d-1}$ indices, so $\|U_j A_NZ-A_NZ\|_1\leq2\|Z\|_1/N$. Passing to the $L^1$ limit gives $U_js=s$. These generators imply invariance under every integer translation. [A1, F2, F5, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 Fix $r\in\mathbb R^d$, put $G=\Lambda_N$, $G'=G+r$, and $B=G\cap G'$. For $N>2\|r\|_\infty$, $B$ contains a cube $J$ of side $N-2\|r\|_\infty$. By [F1] and restriction monotonicity, $D(P_G\Vert Q_G)\leq\gamma N^d$ and $D(P_B\Vert Q_B)\geq D(P_J\Vert Q_J)$; the latter divided by $N^d$ tends to $\gamma$. Therefore $N^{-d}(D(P_G\Vert Q_G)-D(P_B\Vert Q_B))\to0$. The conditional chain rule [F3] identifies $\log h_G-\log h_B$ with a conditional log density. Its mean is this entropy difference, and [F3] bounds its negative-part expectation by $1/e$; thus its $L^1(P)$ norm is at most the entropy difference plus $2/e$. The same bound applies to $G'$. Translation covariance gives $\log h_{G'}=(\log h_G)\circ T_{-r}$; thus the normalized information in $G$ and $G'$ have the same $L^1$ limit. Since $N^{-d}\log h_G\to s$, it follows that $s\circ T_{-r}=s$ $P$-almost surely for this $r$. [A1, F1, F3, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 Step 5.1 applies to every fixed $r\in\mathbb R^d$. For each rational $q$, the event $\{s\leq q\}$ is therefore invariant modulo null sets under every translation. Full-translation ergodicity makes each such event have probability $0$ or $1$. If $s$ were not almost surely constant, some rational sublevel set would have probability strictly between $0$ and $1$; hence $s$ is constant. Its mean from step 4.1 is $\gamma$, so $s=\gamma$. Combining with step 2.1 proves the asserted $L^1(P)$ limit. [A1, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. For stationary finite-intensity configuration laws, let $I(P)$ be relative entropy density with respect to the independent unit-intensity Poisson law, $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$, and $\Phi(P)$ the limiting positional energy density. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are part of the proof below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, HB, a superstable regular pair potential, $z,\beta>0$, and the unit-intensity Poisson reference.

[A1] The choice assumptions are carried explicitly because [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]] uses AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB for compactness and sequential compactness.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]: superstable means a stable part plus a nonnegative repulsive core, regularity supplies the decreasing integrable lower and upper tail, and $Z_Q$ uses normalized unit-intensity Poisson measure.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-superstable-cell-energy-bound]]: there are $A>0,B\geq0$ such that $H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_iN_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega)$.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]: for every finite $c$, the laws with $I(P)\leq c$ are compact and sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ under the assumptions in [A1].

[F4] [[thm-tdmath-spatial-mean-information]]: if a stationary law is ergodic under all translations and has finite $I(P)=\gamma$, then $L^{-d}\log(dP_{\Lambda_L}/dQ_{\Lambda_L})\to\gamma$ in $L^1(P)$.

[F5] [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]: $\tau_L$ is convergence of expectations of every measurable local observable bounded by a constant times $1+N_A$ on some bounded set $A$.

[F6] [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]: for the regular tail class here, the free-cube grand partition is finite and its free pressure limit exists.

[F8] [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]] and [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: finite-region entropy has the conditional chain rule, is nonnegative, and its variational formula applies to bounded measurable tests.

[L1] Georgii's Theorem 1 (1994, Section 3) states that for a superstable lower-regular pair potential, $\Phi(P)=\lim L^{-d}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ exists in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ for every stationary finite-intensity law and is lower semicontinuous in the local topology. Its hypotheses match [F1]–[F2]; the full 1994 proof was read. This supplies the energy-density existence interface, not a certification stamp.

[L2] Georgii's Theorem 2 (1994, Section 3, equations (2.20)–(2.22)) states that for a superstable regular potential and $z,\beta>0$, the free and periodic normalized-Poisson partition functions have the same limiting rate $p(z,\beta)=-\min_P[I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z]$, and the associated rate functional has compact local-tame sublevel sets. ## Proof

**Given:** The assumptions and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Georgii's Theorem 1 [L1] gives existence of $\Phi(P)$ and lower semicontinuity for every stationary finite-intensity law. Its Euclidean radial tail hypothesis follows from ours: $|x|_\infty\leq|x|_2\leq\sqrt d\,|x|_\infty$, so replacing $\psi(r)$ by $\psi(r/\sqrt d)$ preserves monotonicity and finite weighted integral by a change of variables. The stable-plus-positive-core definition matches the source's superstable condition after choosing a smaller Euclidean core ball. Thus $\Phi$ has exactly the domain and convention in the Statement. [F1, F2, L1, algebra]

1.2 The cell estimate [F2] and $\beta>0$ imply $J=I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$ is lower semicontinuous and coercive on bounded-$J$ sets: the Poisson entropy variational inequality with bounded truncations of $aN_{C_0}$ gives $I(P)\geq a\rho(P)-(e^a-1)$; the pointwise square inequality gives $E_PN_{C_0}^2\geq\rho(P)^2$. A finite candidate exists: take independent Bernoulli occupancy of widely separated small cubes, at most one absolutely continuously distributed point per cube, and a uniform random lattice phase. Each tile has finite relative entropy to Poisson, and the summable regular tail bounds its absolute intertile energy per volume. Thus $J$ is proper. Its upper proof uses this entropy identity, block stationarization, and the superstable cell cutoff; its lower proof conditions finite blocks on bounded finite-energy events, inserts empty corridors, and applies the spatial likelihood limit. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F5, F8, L1, L2, step 1.1]

2.2 The minimum is attained: a minimizing sequence lies in a finite sublevel by the sparse finite candidate in step 1.2; compactness [F3] gives a convergent subsequence and lower semicontinuity from step 1.1 gives a minimizer. ## Statement

Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Superstability and regularity, $z>0$, the unit-intensity Poisson reference, and the explicitly defined hard-admissibility beta-zero weight.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]: the interaction is an even measurable superstable pair potential with a decreasing integrable two-sided far-tail envelope, and its normalized Poisson partition uses $1/N!$.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]: stationary laws with bounded Poisson specific entropy are compact in $\tau_L$; $I$ is lower semicontinuous.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-spatial-mean-information]]: for stationary laws ergodic under all translations and with finite specific entropy, normalized finite-volume log likelihoods converge in probability to $I(P)$.


[F4] [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]: for bounded $f$, $D(P\Vert Q)\geq E_Pf-\log E_Qe^f$, and relative entropy has the conditional chain rule and is nonnegative.

[F5] [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]]: for positive inverse temperature the stationary entropy-energy functional has compact sublevels, its free and periodic pressures agree, and finite-energy stationary laws admit separated-block approximation with the stated entropy and local-tame controls.

[F6] [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]: $\tau_L$ tests every measurable local observable bounded by a constant times $1+N_A$.

[F7] [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]: the unit-cube Poisson count has exponential moment $E_Qe^{aN_C}=e^{e^a-1}$, and bounded truncations increase to this count test.

[F8] [[lem-tdmath-periodic-law-local-tame-transfer]]: torus-invariant finite-volume laws with bounded entropy density have relatively compact continued laws, uniformly integrable local counts, and limit entropy bounded by the limiting finite-volume entropy density.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Regularity bounds $\phi$ above outside a bounded set, so $B$ is bounded. Define $\chi=+\infty$ on $B$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then $\chi$ is even, stable with constant $0$, and has zero far tail. Its finite-volume beta-zero partition is exactly the specified hard-admissibility partition. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 For each bounded region $A$, the event that $A$ contains a forbidden pair is a bounded measurable local event. Its probability is continuous under $\tau_L$ by [F6]. Exhausting space by countably many bounded cubes shows that $\mathcal K_B$ is $\tau_L$-closed. Apply [F4] to the bounded tests $f_M=a\min(N_C,M)$ and let $M\to\infty$. Monotone convergence and [F7] give $I(P)\geq a\rho(P)-(e^a-1)$, hence $\rho(P)\leq(I(P)+e^a-1)/a$. Choosing $a>2\max(\log z,0)$ makes $I(P)-\rho(P)\log z$ coercive in $I(P)$. By [F2], every finite sublevel is compact and lower semicontinuous, so the infimum on $\mathcal K_B$ is attained whenever the admissible class is nonempty. The empty configuration law gives a finite candidate. [F2, F4, F6, F7, algebra]

1.3 Fix $P\in\mathcal K_B$ with $I(P)<\infty$. Condition its restriction to a cube of side $n$ on configurations whose distinct points have separation at least $1/q$ and whose finite pair energies are at most $q$. As $q\to\infty$, these events increase to probability one because configurations are locally finite, simple, and hard-admissible. Choose $q=q(n)$ so the conditioning probability tends to one. Tile space by these conditioned blocks separated by an empty corridor wider than the range of $B$ and the fixed tail cutoff, take independent copies, then average the lattice phase uniformly. No cross-block pair is forbidden. The conditional entropy inequality $$ D(P(\cdot\mid E)\Vert Q)\leq [D(P\Vert Q)+1]/P(E)-\log P(E) $$ follows by expanding the conditional density $1_E(dP/dQ)/P(E)$ and using $-u\log u\leq1/e$. Additivity on independent blocks and the vanishing corridor fraction give $\limsup I(P_n)\leq I(P)$; local count truncation and finite first moments give $P_n\to P$ in $\tau_L$. Each $P_n$ has finite original energy density. [F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 For a finite-volume beta-zero Gibbs law $G_L^b$, direct integration of its density gives $$ -\log Z_{Q,L}=D(G_L^b\Vert Q_L)-(\log z)E_{G_L^b}N_L. $$ Stationarize independent blocks and average their phase. The entropy chain rule bounds the resulting specific entropy by the displayed finite-volume entropy per volume; hard admissibility passes to every local limit. Compactness [F2], lower semicontinuity, and the entropy identity therefore give the pressure upper bound by the negative minimum in the statement. For the reverse bound, use the approximating finite-energy laws from step 1.3. Their independent separated blocks are admissible; the spatial likelihood theorem [F3] supplies typical blocks with likelihood cost $I(P_n)$, while empirical counts converge to $\rho(P_n)$. Changing from Poisson measure to the beta-zero weight gives the lower rate $-I(P_n)+\rho(P_n)\log z$. Let $n\to\infty$ and optimize over $P$. Corridors change the normalized log weight by their vanishing volume fraction, so free and periodic rates agree. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two distinct stationary minimizers $P_0,P_1$ with finite equal minimum $m$.

[F1] [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]]: $\Phi(P)$ is the limit of normalized finite-volume expected energies, and $\rho(P)$ is expected unit-cell count.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]]: $I(P)$ is the large-cube limit of relative entropies against the unit-intensity Poisson reference.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-and-chain-rules]]: relative entropy obeys the mixture-label chain rule and is nonnegative.

[F4] [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]: $\tau_L$ tests every bounded measurable local observable.

## Verification

**Given:** The assumptions above.

1.1 Let $P,R$ be stationary laws of finite specific entropy and let $P_\theta=\theta P+(1-\theta)R$. For a bounded cube $G$, the binary-label chain rule [F3] gives $$ \theta D(P_G\Vert Q_G)+(1-\theta)D(R_G\Vert Q_G) =D((P_\theta)_G\Vert Q_G)+I(S;X_G), $$ where $S$ is the mixture label and $X_G$ the observed configuration. Since $0\leq I(S;X_G)\leq H(S)<\infty$, divide by $|G|$ and take the cube limit [F2]; $H(S)/|G|\to0$, so $I(P_\theta)=\theta I(P)+(1-\theta)I(R)$. The expectation defining $\rho$ is affine. For finite energy densities, $E_{P_\theta}H_G=\theta E_PH_G+(1-\theta)E_RH_G$ for every $G$; dividing by volume and taking limits gives affinity of $\Phi$. Thus $J$ is affine on finite mixtures of finite-$J$ laws. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Applying step 1.1 to $P_0,P_1$ gives $J(P_\theta)=\theta J(P_0)+(1-\theta)J(P_1)=m$, so every mixture is a minimizer. Put $P_{2n}=P_0$ and $P_{2n+1}=P_1$. The even and odd subsequences converge locally to $P_0$ and $P_1$. Since distinct laws differ on a bounded-region measurable event, its indicator is a bounded local test by [F4] with different expectations; the full sequence therefore has no $\tau_L$ limit. Both accumulation points are minimizers. [given, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Example

For intensity $z>0$, let $P=Q_z$ be the translation-invariant Poisson law from [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], compared with the unit-intensity reference $Q=Q_1$. Its specific relative entropy is
$$I(Q_z)=1-z+z\log z.$$
The parameter $z$ is a mathematical intensity relative to the chosen reference; no physical preparation is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $d\geq1$, $z>0$, and $P=Q_z$ with reference $Q=Q_1$.

[F1] The cell count under $Q_\lambda$ is Poisson with mean $\lambda$, conditional positions have the same uniform law for all $\lambda$, and disjoint cells are independent ([[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]]).

[F2] Finite-region relative entropy is computed from a Radon–Nikodym density, and the specific entropy is the normalized cube limit ([[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]], [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]]).

[F3] $e^x e^y=e^{x+y}$, $n!=n(n-1)!$ for $n\geq1$, and $e^x=\sum_{n\geq0}x^n/n!$ ([[thm-exponential-addition-formula]], [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]).

## Verification

**Given:** The hypotheses and the laws in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 In one unit cell, the conditional distribution of point positions given the count is identical for $Q_z$ and $Q_1$. The ratio of their count probabilities at $n$ is $$\frac{e^{-z}z^n/n!}{e^{-1}/n!}=e^{1-z}z^n.$$ Thus this is the Radon–Nikodym density on that cell. [F1, algebra]

2.1 The cube $\Lambda_m=[0,m)^d$ is the disjoint union of $m^d$ unit cells. Independence in [F1] makes the finite-cube density the product of the cell densities: $$h_m(\omega)=e^{(1-z)m^d}z^{N_{\Lambda_m}(\omega)}.$$ [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The count $N_{\Lambda_m}$ is Poisson with mean $zm^d$ by [F1]. Directly from its mass function and the exponential series, $$E_PN_{\Lambda_m}=e^{-zm^d}\sum_{n\geq1}n\frac{(zm^d)^n}{n!}=zm^d e^{-zm^d}\sum_{k\geq0}\frac{(zm^d)^k}{k!}=zm^d.$$ Therefore [F2] gives $$\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})}{m^d}=\frac{E_P\log h_m}{m^d}=1-z+z\log z$$ for every positive integer $m$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Taking the cube limit in [F2] yields $I(Q_z)=1-z+z\log z$. At $z=1$ the value is zero, the reference-law baseline. [F2, step 3.1] ∎
